title: John J. Appleton → John Quincy Adams, Cadiz, despatch with an 18-group coded passage on the Spanish liberal government's secret English loan, printed 'no decodification'
correspondents: John James Appleton (US chargé d'affaires ad interim at Madrid, with the Cortes at Cadiz) → John Quincy Adams, Secretary of State
shelfmark: NARA RG 59, Despatches from US Ministers to Spain, vol. 22 (20 May 1822-30 Dec 1823) = microfilm M31 reel 24, catalog naId 188609418
folio_note: 18 code groups in the body (Manning prints them: 1088 648 1576 794 1384 1453 347 1372 500 192 668 1384 169 1244 1501 1110 1426 1290; several OCR-uncertain); frame not located Frame located 27 Oct 2026 (NARA bulk scan, research/nara_triage_a/): M31 reel 24, frame 0134.
status: Manning, Diplomatic Correspondence ... Independence of the Latin-American Nations (1925) vol. 3, doc. 1124, p. 2041, prints the groups with '[no decodification]'. The groups fit the code rebuilt in targets/jqa (the = 1385, of = 1576, that = 1384, and = 668; the London/St Petersburg code): with targets/jqa/code_table.tsv 16 of 18 groups take a value ('... of [794] that ... was [192] and that he had a part in England'). Not in the repo (known.py: Appleton no hits).
why: The Spanish constitutional government's secret plan to raise money in England in the last weeks of the Cortes at Cadiz (1823), told to the US chargé by the finance minister Yandiola; directly readable with a key this repository already holds.
source: NARA RG 59 diplomatic despatches (via Manning 1925) sweep
prior_art: open (checked 27 Oct 2026: Manning prints it undecoded; no other decoding found)

title: Joel Roberts Poinsett → James Monroe, Santiago de Chile, despatch with at least nine cipher passages printed as '(undeciphered cipher)'
correspondents: Joel Roberts Poinsett (US special agent and consul general for Buenos Aires, Chile and Peru) → James Monroe, Secretary of State
shelfmark: NARA RG 59, Despatches from Special Agents, vol. 3 (Poinsett 1813-23) = microfilm M37 roll 2, catalog naId 213803757; Poinsett's other 1811-14 reports ('parts in cipher') are in the Poinsett Papers vol. 4, Historical Society of Pennsylvania (Gilpin collection)
folio_note: nine '(undeciphered cipher)' insertions in Manning's text, single words to whole clauses (on the Carreras, the Buenos Aires army, the Portuguese, the Araucanian chief); frame of the letter not located (M37 roll 2 frames 16-24 are the Poinsett list and his 'State of society' essay) Frame located 27 Oct 2026 (research/nara_triage_a/): M37 roll 2, frame 0093; a coded sibling of 14 June 1814 is at frames 0097-0099.
status: Manning 1925 vol. 2, doc. 442, pp. 896-897, prints the despatch with '(undeciphered cipher)' at each coded passage; the State Department returned Poinsett's other letters to him in 1818, so his own copies (some 'Part in cipher', May-July 1811 from Buenos Aires, per the HSP list filmed at M37 roll 2 frames 20-22) are at HSP, possibly with plaintext drafts. Not in the repo (known.py: Poinsett no hits). Worked 28 Oct 2026 (targets/poinsett1813, write-up poinsett1813): 437 groups transcribed; the same-code letter of 14 June 1814 (no. 651) carries a clerk's decipherment, 95 values, 161 of 437 groups of 1813 get a value, no sentence reads. Other State Department rolls searched (M37 1-2, M70, M77, M84): no further letter in the code.
why: Poinsett was an active partisan of the Carreras in the first Chilean republic; the hidden passages are his own views on the Chilean leadership and the war with Peru, otherwise unrecorded in US files.
source: NARA RG 59 diplomatic despatches (via Manning 1925) sweep
prior_art: open (checked 27 Oct 2026: Manning; web search found no decipherment)

title: José Rafael Revenga → Colombian Secretary of Foreign Affairs, Madrid, letter partly in cipher intercepted by the French, sent to Washington by Anderson with no key
correspondents: José Rafael Revenga (Colombian envoy in Spain) → Pedro Gual, Secretary of Foreign Affairs of Colombia (paper enclosed by Richard C. Anderson, US minister at Bogotá → John Quincy Adams)
date: 1822 (duplicate intercepted in France; delivered at Bogotá, transmitted 19 Jan 1824)
shelfmark: NARA RG 59, Despatches from US Ministers to Colombia, vol. 3, enclosure 'No. 4' (paper in fragments) to Anderson's despatch of 19 Jan 1824 (microfilm T33)
folio_note: a paper in fragments, written partly in cipher; Manning: 'Not printed. A postscript to Anderson's letter explains that no key to the cipher was furnished. The portions not in cipher are, alone, unintelligible.'
status: Manning 1925 vol. 2, doc. 641, pp. 1272-73. Gual told Anderson it was the duplicate of a Revenga letter from Madrid sent through France, intercepted and opened there, then handed by Count Landos (a French agent at Cartagena, 1822) to a Colombian agent. Revenga's other cipher letters (Archivo General de la Nación, Bogotá; Archivo Santander) may share the key. Not in the repo (known.py: Revenga no hits). 27 Oct 2026 (WAINUT, PR #109; targets/revenga1822/, in progress): key recovered from the ciphertext alone; deciphered in part on a first-pass transcription of the four frames.
why: Colombia's first envoy to Spain reporting on the 1822 negotiations for recognition, a letter the French secret service read and the Colombians passed to the US to warn of French designs.
source: NARA RG 59 diplomatic despatches (via Manning 1925) sweep
prior_art: open (checked 27 Oct 2026: Manning)

title: German Army Truppenschlüssel messages, net 'pz6', 4 July 1941 (Nr. 88, 90, 91, 92, 94, 97; also 95, 96 same day)
correspondents: German Army front-line units (call sign pz6) → same net
shelfmark: German Army message collection (original message forms, provenance given only as the German Army message collection; the BGAC page names the Bundesarchiv for its 2026 finds); transcribed by Olaf Ostwald and Frode Weierud
folio_note: Six pz6 messages 35+96+88+126+143+59 = 547 letters, plus Nr. 95 (74) and Nr. 96 (62) with blank addressee; facsimiles for Nr. 88, 94, 95
status: CryptoCellar 1941 Message List (status 20 Oct 2026) marks 24 of the 30 messages broken in Sept 2026 (Paefgen; Davies, Willis, Khan, marked AI), DOLHA 252 only in part; pz6 Nr. 88-97 by Paefgen 21.09 and Davies 25.09; plaintexts not published. Still unbroken: EHNPZ 123 (8 Jul, net 4fc), AFUVO 26, ZUBZE 8, MZXNX 21, AAXYN 31, AOXST 91; also BCUCC Nr. 20 NF (5 Sep 1941), not in this row. See targets/ts1941pz6/ (WAINUT, PR #125; ciphertext-only attempt failed; Status: no write-up). Earlier: Listed as unbroken on CryptoCellar 'Unbroken German Army Truppenschlüssel Messages' (updated 27 Jul 2026). Truppenschlüssel is a hand cipher (simplified Doppelkasten); most of the 100+ surviving TS messages were broken by Ostwald & Weierud (Cryptologia 2021). Not in the repo (only Enigma rows of this collection are on HCPortal; Cryptoole's CryptoCellar rows were dropped wholesale as Enigma). This entry covers all 30 unbroken 1941 Truppenschlüssel messages on the CryptoCellar list, by net: net 'pz6', 4 July 1941 (Nr. 88, 90, 91, 92, 94, 97; also 95, 96 same day); net 'nfw', 3 July 1941 (Nr. 84, 85, 86); net '4fc', 8 July 1941 (Nr. 123, 129, 130); net 'f8y', 6 and 8 July 1941 (Nr. 109, 110, 121); net '8be', 25 July 1941 (Nr. 263, 264); June-September 1941 (VHRNE Nr. 284, AOXST Nr. 91, XWFEC Nr. 193, MZXNX Nr. 21, AAXYN Nr. 31, DOLHA Nr. 252, LSSLG Nr. 268, ZUBZE Nr. 8, CFQIB Nr. 281, YSGSS Nr. 56, AFUVO Nr. 26). They were dropped from the 14 Oct Cryptoole import because research/cryptoole/pull.py filtered every CryptoCellar row as Enigma.
why: A same-day, same-net group of a WWII hand field cipher left unbroken by modern cryptanalysis: a direct test case for the paper beside the Orpo Doppelkasten target.
prior_art: broken by others Sept 2026 for 24/30 (CryptoCellar 1941 Message List, status 20 Oct 2026); unpublished; checked 27 Oct 2026

title: Communist Party of America underground: book-cipher addresses and names in letters seized at 170 Bleecker St., New York, 1920-21
correspondents: District organizers and members (signing D.O. 5, J. Mortin, Frederick Mayer ...) ↔ the Executive Secretary ("EXSEC", Paul Holt), Communist Party of America
shelfmark: NARA RG 65, Investigative Case Files of the Bureau of Investigation 1908-1922, Old German Files (M1085) roll 940, case 202600 ("202600-1775 THRU 202600-1949-1 (4 of 4)", naId 369272950), multi-page PDFs M1085-940A, -940B, -940C ("Copies of Letters & Documents Found at 170 Bleecker St.")
folio_note: OCR count: 77 runs of line/letter fraction groups (e.g. "(New code) 3/3 3/4 2/8 3/7 1/14 - 7/3 2/7 4/4 ...", "Old code P 14 ... 14/15 2/1 6/4"), about 2,400 fraction tokens over the three PDFs. 27 runs are followed by a Bureau "Decode:" or "the above code reads as follows" line; about 50 runs show no decode nearby. 940C also copies the party's own instruction for the system (count lines down, letters across on a set page; a dash between words).
status: Seen in the OCR of the digitised reel: Bureau agents copied the seized letters and decoded many of the coded addresses (class A: decodes in the same file give cribs for the page). The undecoded runs are names, addresses and telegraph covers. Not on DECODE; nothing in the repo. 27 Oct 2026 (WAINUT, PR #116; targets/cpa1920/, in progress): 28 runs and 439 tokens on the typed pages (the 77 runs / 2,400 tokens of the OCR count also took in dates and ratios); handwritten pages not yet searched. Key grid rebuilt from the Bureau's own decodes of 16 runs; the book is not identified.
why: The early US Communist underground (after the Palmer raids) hid its contact network in a book code; the undecoded runs would name more of that network, and the system is a clean example of a period book cipher.

title: Col. Williams, Allied Mine Guard → Commanding General AEF Siberia: enciphered field message No. 5, Vladimirovka
correspondents: Col. Williams, Commanding Officer, Allied Mine Guard (31st Infantry) → Commanding General, American Expeditionary Force Siberia, Vladivostok
shelfmark: NARA RG 395, Records of US Army Overseas Operations and Commands, AEF Siberia historical files, microfilm M917 roll 9 (file unit naId 337865023, "21-33.5 Headquarters, AEF in Siberia"), frame M917-009-0963
folio_note: One US Army Field Message form: 32 five-letter groups (160 letters), beginning LJEQE WJJOM RFAHN OVLBO, ending XXKOX XALYX (X padding). Note: 'Given to Japanese Captain 7/8/19 ... to be sent to Vladivostok by wireless'. Filed as an appendix to the Mine Guard war diary between clear field messages Nos. 2 and 4 of 7-8 July and No. 1 of 9 July.

links.label: clear text: M917 roll 6 file unit

status: Enciphered text; probable clear text found (GitHub issue 202, Harumi-Matsuba, 31 Oct 2026, checked on the images here the same day). The receiving headquarters filed its decoded copy as Inclosure VI to Intelligence Summary No. 228, NARA RG 395, M917 roll 6 (naId 337862017), frame M917-006-0919: 'Official copy of telegram received at Vladivostok 9:30 PM ... July 9, 1919 ... VLADIMIRO. Commanding General Amexforce. No. 5. July 9th. Leaving Vladimiro for Souchan this date with supplies, a detachment will return to Vladimiro following day. If practicable will meet Major Cutrer's column near Kazanka. WILLIAMS', with a 'Decoded by' line and handwritten initials. Number, date, sender, addressee and same-evening wireless receipt match frame M917-009-0963. The match rests on those headers: the 32 cipher groups (160 letters) have not been reproduced from the clear text (about 148 letters without padding; the cipher has no G or Z, the clear copy has both), and the headquarters copy may be a paraphrase. Tests reported in the issue, all negative: Beaufort cipher disk with periodic key (period 2-89, known plaintext at every offset, including reversed text, words and clauses), key changing every 2-8 letters, autokey, digraphic, transposition alone, transposition with periodic substitution (period 1-12). Not tested here: an enciphered code (MI-8 or other 1918-19 AEF code), which is the likeliest remaining reading. Earlier tests of 27 Oct 2026 (vig1919.py): IC 0.041, no periodic Vigenere/Beaufort period 2-15, JJ inside a digraph. Not in catalogue.json before the NARA triage (known.py).
why: A field cipher of the US intervention in Siberia, sent through Japanese wireless during the July 1919 partisan fighting round the Suchan mines; it shows which system the AEF Siberia used in the field.
